insight.title: Why You Scrutinize Small Details and Ignore Big Risks
insight.subtitle: How solving easy problems prevents you from making real progress

sections.text: Have you ever noticed how a tiny expense gets more scrutiny than a massive strategic shift? Your brain prefers "solvable" problems over complex ones, creating a hidden system that prioritizes comfort over impact.

This is the Law of Triviality. We obsess over small details because we understand them perfectly. This creates a false sense of progress while the truly difficult, high-leverage challenges remain unaddressed and growing.

In business, this looks like debating a minor policy for hours while ignoring a shift in consumer behavior. By winning these easy battles, you exhaust the mental energy required to navigate your larger strategy.
Try this today: When you analyze a small problem today, ask if it truly changes your trajectory.
The easiest things to fix are rarely the things worth fixing.

debug.angle: focus on how small things create bigger effects

brazil.description: SAO PAULO, May 2 - Heavy rains that hit northeastern Brazil over the last 48 hours have killed at least six people and displaced thousands in the states of Pernambuco and Paraiba, the federal government said in a statement on Saturday.

south_korea.title: South Korea’s April exports rise 48% as chip boom extends
south_korea.description: Semiconductor and computer-related exports surge, offsetting weaker autos and higher energy costs.

japan.title: Core inflation in Tokyo slows, seen accelerating on energy shock
japan.description: The Tokyo core CPI, which excludes volatile fresh food costs, rose 1.5% in April from a year earlier.

japan.title: Why Japan-China ties can benefit from promoting people-to-people exchanges
japan.description: Japan and China are Asian powerhouses that should collaborate responsibly for the peace and prosperity of the region. mexico.title: Mexican governor and mayor indicted by US for drug trafficking step down
mexico.description: They both are members of Mexican President Sheinbaum s party in Sinaloa state.

alternates.title: Mexican governor steps aside after US accusations of cartel ties
alternates.description: MEXICO CITY, May 2 - The governor of Mexico's Sinaloa state, who has been accused by the U.S. of aiding one of the country's most powerful drug cartels, said on Friday he would step down temporarily as a local investigation into the charges proceeds.

alternates.title: Mexico’s Sinaloa state governor resigns amid US drug trafficking charges
alternates.description: Ruben Rocha Moya again denies allegations he shielded cartel, says taking temporary leave to defend self.
